text: Vaccination (ការចាក់វ៉ាក់សាំង) is an important part of disease prevention (ការការពារជំងឺ) but works alongside -- not instead of -- good nutrition, clean water, housing, hygiene, biosecurity, and responsible animal movement. The right vaccination program depends on species, age, production purpose, prior vaccination history, local disease occurrence, and current veterinary guidance -- cattle, pigs, and poultry need different strategies, and a chicken schedule should never be applied to ducks or vice versa. Vaccines are biological products that can lose effectiveness outside their required temperature range; smallholders with limited refrigeration should coordinate vaccination through a veterinarian, animal-health worker, or cooperative rather than storing vaccines indefinitely at home. During the wet season, muddy conditions make hygiene harder; during the dry season, heat and unreliable electricity threaten the cold chain needed for vaccine storage. Keep a simple vaccination record (animal/flock, vaccine name, date, batch if available). CRITICAL RULE: never generate a vaccine dose, dilution, injection route, age, timing, or booster interval as a universal fact -- these are product- and disease-specific and must come from a veterinarian, competent animal-health professional, or the current registered product label. Do not name a specific Cambodian vaccination calendar or assume a particular breed for Preah Vihear -- disease priorities and official programs change, and breed has less influence on vaccination needs than species, age, and disease risk.
